package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in this report. The article discusses general software supply chain risks, the need for transparency, and the importance of detecting malicious code, but does not analyze or provide details about any particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network communications during build or install processes
Tampering with build or release pipelines
Inclusion of unknown or suspicious dependencies (typosquatting)
Code that exfiltrates environment variables or sensitive files
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious third-party packages
Unexpected modifications to build scripts or pipeline configuration files
Unexplained changes in SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted or unknown domains during build or install
Unexpected API calls to external services from build environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity and file access during build, install, and runtime phases. Use automated tools to analyze all code (first-, second-, and third-party) for signs of tampering or malware. Require and review SBOMs and secure development attestations from all vendors. Flag and investigate any package or vendor unwilling to provide transparency or attestations.
